rule: ONE fact, ONE owner, and the generated file stays generated. An adjudication RESULT is authored by a human after M14.0.F11 has run; it is recorded HERE and never written into validation/m60/grammar-survey.json, which is regenerated wholesale by script/m60/build-grammar-survey.ts. The first version of this work recorded refusals directly into the generated survey, and the next regeneration silently erased three of them — the same two-sources-one-truth defect this milestone exists to close, recreated one level up. The generator MERGES this file in, and a ruling here that matches no candidate is a hard failure rather than a silent loss.
whatBelongsHere: A verdict (refused | admitted | superseded) with the review document that justifies it, the instrument that produced it, the measured numbers it rests on, and the screening measurement. It does NOT belong here: the lane universe, versions, upstream state, candidate discovery, or damage measurements — those are the generator's, derived from the repository and from npm/GitHub.
gate: C6 in script/m60/verify-grammar-consistency.ts requires a non-default verdict in the survey to name a review document that exists on disk. It cannot check this file, because this file is the input to that verdict; the generator is what makes the two agree.

rulings.confound: This A/B is 0.3.12 against OUR PATCHED 0.3.11, so part of G3 measures the absence of our two rules (module_val_declaration, nullable_type) and not 0.3.12's own quality. The battery carries the weight instead: 0.3.12 adds nothing we would want, so there is no reason to port the patch onto it.
rulings.knownLimit: --sample 400 does not complete: the G2 s-expression comparison dies with `call_indirect to a signature that does not match` at C._ts_node_to_string_wasm. NOT an ABI mismatch — all three wasms report language.version 15 and toString() succeeds on all three for a trivial parse. It is input-dependent: the fsharp grammar exhausts the fixed web-tree-sitter heap on the compiler's largest files, the same fragility that appears as a ts_malloc_default abort when walking the 6,627-file corpus. Future fsharp grammar decisions are gated at --sample 250 or below, with the sample stated so two runs are comparable.

recovery.note: no concentrated loss and 23 files gain; the +180% error-NODE reading is not treated as damage because for this grammar error-node count is a known-bad proxy (a previous build hid ~1,000 errors inside one 1,900-line ERROR node) while F11's per-file error-LINE figure is the usable one.

rulings.candidateProvenance: fetched, rebuilt from source with tree-sitter CLI 0.26.9, and the rebuild reproduced the published prebuilt BYTE-FOR-BYTE (79612413..., 1,088,467 B) — so the adjudicated artifact is provably upstream's
rulings.pinnedProvenance: wasm/tree-sitter-powershell.wasm sha256 1d30b5a2..., 983,236 B is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the npm tarball wasm of tree-sitter-powershell@0.25.10 (2025-12-08). The lane shipped its whole life with no version recorded anywhere; that debt is now closed and written into docs/analyzers/powershell.md.
rulings.whyNoF11: The corpus cannot carry an A/B verdict. Of the PowerShell repository's 553 tracked .ps1, 182 carry grammar errors and 166 of those are the repo's OWN intentionally-invalid parser-error test fixtures (unexpectedErrorFiles: 0). G1's 'newly damaged' would fire on a file designed to fail, for either grammar. The discriminating population is the 16 named limits. F11's LANES still gained a powershell entry so a gated verdict remains available; it is simply not the right first instrument here.

battery.note: 6 of the constructs the M12 artifact names for a file PARSE STANDALONE, so the construct recorded as that file's cause is not what breaks it — a second defect, in the evidence rather than the grammar. Those are excluded from the denominator, because counting them would inflate the limit count and flatter any candidate.

recovery.note: neutral to marginally better on the broad corpus — the same 'not worse, not different' shape fsharp 0.3.12 showed. Being behind is not the problem; the newer release does not contain the constructs this lane fails on.
